subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should cron jobs get a supervisor-visible lifecycle watchdog for started-but-no-terminal runs when Gateway memory pressure can block the in-process failureAlert path?
rationale: Current code can mark interrupted runs after restart, but choosing an alert path that survives a wedged Gateway changes the product boundary between cron state, gateway supervision, and operator notification.

options.title: Add supervisor-visible lifecycle reporting
options.body: Persist started and terminal cron transitions in a way a restart or external supervisor can turn missing terminal state into an operator-visible failure.

options.title: Limit scope to memory stability
options.body: Treat failureAlert silence as secondary and only keep this issue for proving and fixing the memory/RSS growth root cause.

options.title: Close after unreproduced soak
options.body: If a current-main macOS soak cannot reproduce growth or silent cron failure, close this issue and file narrower reports for any new evidence.

recommendation.title: Add supervisor-visible lifecycle reporting
recommendation.body: Persist started and terminal cron transitions in a way a restart or external supervisor can turn missing terminal state into an operator-visible failure.

likelyOwner.reason: The open product question centers on cron lifecycle and restart recovery behavior, where recent related history points to yetval.
